The purple one might make you hungry, and it also includes a classic Connections letter-addition trick. If you need help, you\'re in the right place. Read on for clues and today\'s Connections answers.The Times now has a Connections Bot, like the one for Wordle. Go there after you play to receive a numeric score and to have the program analyze your answers. Players who are registered with the Times Games section can now nerd out by following their progress, including the number of puzzles completed, win rate, number of times they nabbed a perfect score and their win streak.Read more:\xa0Hints, Tips and Strategies to Help You Win at NYT Connections Every TimeHints for today\'s Connections groupsHere are four hints for the groupings in today\'s Connections puzzle, ranked from the easiest yellow group to the tough (and sometimes bizarre) purple group.Yellow group hint: Tip over.Green group hint: Time to read.Blue group hint: Think tantrums.Purple group hint: Trick-or-treat treats, with a different letter.Answers for today\'s Connections groupsYellow group: Topple.Green group: Part of a book.Blue group: Lose it, with "out."Purple group: Chocolate bars plus a letter.Read more: Wordle Cheat Sheet: Here Are the Most Popular Letters Used in English WordsWhat are today\'s Connections answers?     The completed NYT Connections puzzle for Oct. 19, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETThe yellow words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is topple. The four answers are fall, spill, tumble and wipeout.The green words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is part of a book. The four answers are cover, jacket, leaves and spine.The blue words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is lose it, with "out." The four answers are bug, flip, freak and wig.The purple words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is chocolate bars plus a letter. The four answers are crunchy, dover, marsh and skort. (Crunch, Dove, Mars and Skor.)Toughest Connections puzzlesWe\'ve made a note of some of the toughest Connections puzzles so far. rose.#3: Included "streets on screen," such as Elm, Fear, Jump and Sesame.#2: Included "power ___" such as nap, plant, Ranger and trip.#1: Included "things that can run," such as candidate, faucet, See full bio    Gael Cooper     \n  Oct. 19, 2025  2:00 a.m. PT 2 min read           Need help with today\'s Strands answers? We\'ve got you. James Martin/CNET    Looking for the most recent Strands answer?\xa0Click here for our daily Strands hints, as well as our daily answers and hints for The New York Times Mini Crossword, Wordle, Connections and Connections: Sports Edition puzzles.Today\'s NYT\xa0Strands\xa0puzzle is a bit tough, but in the end, pretty fun. Once I figured out the theme, I could unscramble the answers pretty easily. But if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0For the picking.If that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: Keeps the doctor away.Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:CARE, RACE, PURE, TOME, TOMES, DRIFT, DISC, TUFT, SUET, FEUD, SEERAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:CIDER, JELLY, SAUCE, BUTTER, COMPOTE, FRITTER, STRUDELToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Oct. 19, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETToday\'s Strands spangram is\xa0APPLES. To find it, look for the A that\'s 5 letters down on the far-left row, and wind across.Toughest Strands puzzlesHere are some of the Strands topics I\'ve found to be the toughest in recent weeks.#1: Dated slang, Jan. 21. Maybe you didn\'t even use this lingo when it was cool. Toughest word: PHAT.#2: Thar she blows! Jan.15. I guess marine biologists might ace this one. Toughest word: BALEEN or RIGHT.\xa0#3: Off the hook, Jan. 9. Similar to the Jan. 15 puzzle in that it helps to know a lot about sea creatures. Sorry, Charlie. Toughest word: BIGEYE or SKIPJACK.     \n    Gaming Guides\n   \n      Virtual Reality Gaming\n     \n  \n          Best VR Headsets\n        \n          Best Meta Quest 2 Games and Experiences\n Some of the answers are a bit tough to unscramble, so if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0Banding togetherIf that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: Rock out.Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:POLE, LOPE, RATS, RATE, RATES, RATER, GATE, GATES, STAG, TAGS, CORE, REOPEN, HEAD, LINE, LINERAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:STAGE, ENCORE, OPENER, HEADLINER, MERCHANDISEToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Oct. 21, 2025. Click here for today\'s Connections hints, as well as our daily answers and hints for The New York Times Mini Crossword, Wordle and Strands puzzles.Today\'s\xa0Connections: Sports Edition\xa0is a fun one. No, "figure" and "8" don\'t go together -- that would be too easy. If you\'re struggling but still want to solve it, read on for hints and the answers.Connections: Sports Edition is published by The Athletic, the subscription-based sports journalism site owned by the Times. It doesn\'t show up in the NYT Games app but appears in The Athletic\'s own app. Or you can play it for free online.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections: Sports Edition Puzzle Comes Out of BetaHints for today\'s Connections: Sports Edition groupsHere are four hints for the groupings in today\'s Connections: Sports Edition puzzle, ranked from the easiest yellow group to the tough (and sometimes bizarre) purple group.Yellow group hint: Fake out an opponent.Green group hint: Beantown.Blue group hint: Famed shortstop.Purple group hint: Let it snow.Answers for today\'s Connections: Sports Edition groupsYellow group: Move to evade a defender.Green group: Boston sports teams.Blue group: Associated with Cal Ripken Jr.Purple group: First words of Winter Olympic sports.Read more: Wordle Cheat Sheet: Here Are the Most Popular Letters Used in English WordsWhat are today\'s Connections: Sports Edition answers?     The completed NYT Connections: Sports Edition puzzle for Oct. 14, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETThe yellow words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is move to evade a defender. The four answers are deke, juke, sidestep and spin.The green words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is Boston sports teams. The four answers are Bruins, Patriots, Red Sox and Revolution.The blue words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is associated with Cal Ripken Jr. The four answers are 8, Iron Man, Orioles and streak.The purple words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is first words of Winter Olympic sports. The four answers are alpine, figure, Nordic and speed.Quick tips for Connections: Sports Edition#1: Don\'t grab for the easiest group. For each word, think about other sports categories it might fit in – is this a word that can be used in football, or to describe scoring options?#2: Second meanings are important. The puzzle loves to use last names and even college names that mean other things, to fool you into thinking they are words, not names.#3: And the opposite is also true. Words like HURTS might seem like a regular word, but it\'s also the last name of at least one pro athlete.     \n    Gaming Guides\n   \n      Virtual Reality Gaming\n     \n  \n          Best VR James Martin/CNET    Looking for the most recent Strands answer?\xa0Click here for our daily Strands hints, as well as our daily answers and hints for The New York Times Mini Crossword, Wordle, Connections and Connections: Sports Edition puzzles.Today\'s NYT\xa0Strands\xa0puzzle is a tricky one. Some of the answers are a bit tough to unscramble, so if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0"It\'s in the mail."If that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: Do people even use this form of payment any more?Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:CHECK, CHECKS, SNARE, SNARES, MITE, SNOG, MOUNT, MESS, DARE, NUMBAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:MEMO, AMOUNT, NUMBER, ROUTING, SIGNATURE, ADDRESSToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Oct. 20, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETToday\'s Strands spangram is\xa0CHECKLIST. As a Vikings and Seahawks fan, I spotted two nicknames for parts of those teams right away. Of course, the purple category is its typically loopy self. If you\'re struggling but still want to solve it, read on for hints and the answers.Connections: Sports Edition is published by The Athletic, the subscription-based sports journalism site owned by The Times. It doesn\'t show up in the NYT Games app but appears in The Athletic\'s own app. Or you can play it for free online.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections: Sports Edition Puzzle Comes Out of BetaHints for today\'s Connections: Sports Edition groupsHere are four hints for the groupings in today\'s Connections: Sports Edition puzzle, ranked from the easiest yellow group to the tough (and sometimes bizarre) purple group.Yellow group hint: Buy me some Cracker Jack.Green group hint: Hoops homes.Blue group hint: Like the Monsters of the Midway.Purple group hint: Football teams, with a twist.Answers for today\'s Connections: Sports Edition groupsYellow group: Things a stadium vendor sells.Green group: NBA arenas.Blue group: Famous nicknames for NFL defenses.Purple group: NFL teams, with the second-to-last letter changed.Read more: Wordle Cheat Sheet: Here Are the Most Popular Letters Used in English WordsWhat are today\'s Connections: Sports Edition answers?     The completed NYT Connections: Sports Edition puzzle for Oct. 29, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETThe yellow words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is things a stadium vendor sells. The four answers are beer, cotton candy, hot dogs and peanuts.The green words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is NBA arenas. The four answers are Barclays, Little Caesars, Smoothie King and United.The blue words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is famous nicknames for NFL defenses. The four answers are Legion of Boom, Orange Crush, Purple People Eaters and Steel Curtain.The purple words in today\'s ConnectionsThe theme is NFL teams, with the second-to-last letter changed. The four answers are beads (Bears), biles (Bills), colas (Colts) and packets (Packers).Quick tips for Connections: Sports Edition#1: Don\'t grab for the easiest group. For each word, think about other sports categories it might fit in – is this a word that can be used in football, or to describe scoring options?#2: Second meanings are important. The puzzle loves to use last names and even college names that mean other things, to fool you into thinking they are words, not names.#3: And the opposite is also true. Words like HURTS might seem like a regular word, but it\'s also the last name of at least one pro athlete.     \n    Gaming Guides\n   \n      Virtual Reality Gaming\n     \n  \n          Best VR Some of the answers are a bit tough to unscramble, so if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0Go the distance.If that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: 26.2 miles.Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints, but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:RUNT, TURN, TURNER, STAT, STAR, HATS, RATS, CAPE, MOTE, STRAT, TART, TARTS, ROAN, DRAT, DRAM, HOME, TOME, TIME, TIMER, PERKAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight, but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:PACE, START, FINISH, RUNNER, HYDRATION, TIMEKEEPERToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Sunday, Nov. 2, 2025. Some of the answers are a bit tough to unscramble, so if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0Going up?If that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: Not an escalator, but...Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:ROTATE, LOBE, NOPE, RATS, STAR, SAME, LOSE, VOTE, BUTTE, SAMS, BAMSAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:ALARM, OPEN, CLOSE, LOBBY, GROUND, BASEMENTToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Oct. 15, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETToday\'s Strands spangram is\xa0ELEVATORBUTTONS. James Martin/CNET    Looking for the most recent Strands answer?\xa0Click here for our daily Strands hints, as well as our daily answers and hints for The New York Times Mini Crossword, Wordle, Connections and Connections: Sports Edition puzzles.Today\'s NYT\xa0Strands\xa0puzzle is a fun one, and it might make you hungry. Some of the answers are a bit tough to unscramble, so if you need hints and answers, read on.I go into depth about the\xa0rules for Strands in this story.\xa0If you\'re looking for today\'s Wordle, Connections and Mini Crossword answers, you can visit\xa0CNET\'s NYT puzzle hints page.Read more:\xa0NYT Connections Turns 1: These Are the 5 Toughest Puzzles So FarHint for today\'s Strands puzzleToday\'s Strands theme is:\xa0It\'s not polite to lick your plateIf that doesn\'t help you, here\'s a clue: Yum!Clue words to unlock in-game hintsYour goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle\'s theme. If you\'re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:VALE, CABLE, ABLE, MUSE, SLED, TALE, ROUSE, ROUSED, COOP, ELECT, TABLE, SCRUMAnswers for today\'s Strands puzzleThese are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the spangram, a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:DELICIOUS, FLAVORFUL, DELECTABLE, SCRUMPTIOUSToday\'s Strands spangram     The completed NYT Strands puzzle for Saturday, Nov. 1, 2025. NYT/Screenshot by CNETToday\'s Strands spangram is GOODTASTE.
